newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Carter Holt, FCL Paper shine as NZ shares end firm.
newsitem.headline: Carter Holt, FCL Paper shine as NZ shares end firm.

text.p: * Shares end mixed, but forestry stocks lead index higher
* Interest in Carter Holt announcement due Thursday
* Air NZ shares weak, Lion falls on Aust market shr comment
Strong gains in forestry stocks Carter Holt Harvey and Fletcher Paper led New Zealand shares to a higher close on Wednesday, but the wider market was mixed.
Jim Patterson at First NZ Capital said the forestry stocks had captured the imagination of some offshore investors who were looking to pick the bottom of the pulp and paper cycle.

Sean Vaughan at County Natwest said there was also some speculation over an announcement by Carter Holt, due on Thursday, of a modernisation of its pulp and paper mill at Kinleith. The stock rose 18 cents to NZ$3.50.

Among the other leaders, Brierley Investments was firm but Telecom slipped a cent on lowish volume. Brewer Lion Nathan closed three cents lower at $3.52 after Chief Executive Douglas Myers told the annual meeting that declining market share in Australia had continued into the first quarter of the current financial year. He said improving performance in the Australian beer market was the company's top priority.
Air New Zealand, which ended strongly on Tuesday after news of a commercial alliance with United Airlines, saw its "A" shares slip eight cents to $2.65, while the "B"s slipped five to $3.65.

Elsewhere, Fletcher Energy was five cents weaker at $4.01, still feeling the effects of disappointing drilling reports. The company said this week it had abandoned part of its Juragan 2B well in Brunei.
